newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigeria protests treatment of citizens over visas.
newsitem.headline: Nigeria protests treatment of citizens over visas.

text.p: Nigeria's military government has protested against the treatment by embassies of its citizens who apply for visas, a Foreign Ministry official said on Thursday.

He said the ministry's director-general, Jibrin Chinade, made the government view known when he met a British High Commission (embassy) representative in the capital Abuja on Wednesday and would convey the same sentiments to the United States embassy.
"The government is very unhappy with the way and manner in which Nigerians who apply for visas are treated by many countries," newspapers quoted Chinade as saying.
He said the two embassies charged hefty fees for visas which were eventually denied after marathon scrutiny of applicants.
Military-ruled Nigeria's relations with Western nations are strained for lack of democracy and alleged human rights abuses.
Nationals of the populous African nation also have a reputation abroad of sharp practices which has made it difficult for even genuine travellers to secure foreign visas.
"If these countries do not want to grant Nigerians visas, at least they should not stamp them because other embassies will reject any application on account of the stamp," Chinade said.
He said this was unacceptable, adding that some embassies made more than three billion naira ($35.2 million) annually from the charges while 75 percent of such applications were turned down.
"Nigerians as people have to be respected in their own country. I have instances when Nigerians have been treated with contempt," he said.
